key_insight: Thermodynamic dislocation theory can be averaged over arbitrary isotropic grain orientations to produce a unified associated J2 plasticity model for general multiaxial loading.
engineering_relevance: The framework predicts tension, compression, and torsion with one physically based parameter set, making it useful for high-rate metal forming and structural simulation across loading paths.
method: Extends equal-probability orientation averaging from axial loading to general macroscopically uniform stress and strain states.
Uses exact isotropic identities to link mean resolved shear stress to von Mises stress and plastic flow direction to the stress deviator.
Keeps dislocation density and effective disorder temperature evolution in time-rate form so arbitrary loading paths can be followed.
evidence_signal: Copper parameters were fit jointly to Hopkinson-bar tension, dynamic compression, and torsion data, matching 142 points from 10 to 2300 s^-1 and room temperature to 1173 K with up to 6% rms error.
watch_item: The model depends on the assumed initial dislocation state, which can affect torsion predictions and must be calibrated carefully for new specimens.
paper_title: Averaging in thermodynamic dislocation theory: general macroscopically uniform stress and strain states
